result.topic_en: A derivation toward Lagrange's inversion theorem for x = t + u·φ(x): the partial derivatives of x with respect to t and u, and the resulting relation ∂f(x)/∂u = ∂/∂t ∫φ(x) df(x).
result.transcription:
Math 22
[-4642-]
(2)
Lagranges Lehrsatz
$x = t + u\varphi x$
x function von t und u
$\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\right) = \frac{1}{1-u\varphi' x}$ $\left(\frac{dx}{du}\right) = \frac{\varphi x}{1-u\varphi' x}$
Also wenn $fx$ irgend eine function von $x$ vorstellt
$\left(\frac{d.fx}{du}\right) = \varphi x \times \left(\frac{\partial . fx}{\partial t}\right)$
Ist also $Fx$ so mit $fx$ verknüpft dass $F'x = \varphi x . f'x$
so wird
$\frac{\partial . fx}{du} = f'x . \frac{dx}{du} = f'x . \varphi x . \frac{\partial x}{dt} = F'x . \frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial . Fx}{dt}$
Man hat also $Fx = \int \varphi x . f'x . dx = \int(\varphi x . \partial fx)$ und
$\frac{\partial . fx}{du} = \frac{\partial . \int \varphi x . dfx}{\partial t}$
